# A bill's grouped payment naming the bank split among its `PaymentSplit`s.
#
# A `Transaction` block's splits have to be ones that settle the record, and
# the bank's guid is on the transaction too — the likeliest one to reach for,
# and nothing else on that path catches it. Nothing here moves a split, so
# sitting on the right account is a precondition rather than something the
# run fixes up.
#
# The refusal names the account the record posts to, and for a bill that is
# the **payable**. Telling its reader to "name the receivable splits" sends
# them looking for an account their book has not got.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the bank split, the payable,
# and the account this bill posts to.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-USD-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-24
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Suspense USD"
    Transaction "4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b"
      PaymentSplit "5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c"
      PaymentSplit "6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d"
